## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Amos 1:1-3:15 is taken as three linked units: (i) the book's title/epigraph (1:1-2), naming Amos and sounding the LORD's own opening roar; (ii) the eight-nation oracle-cycle (1:3-2:16) — Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab, Judah, Israel, in that fixed order, each following the "three transgressions... four" formula, escalating from international violence (six foreign nations) through general covenant-infidelity (Judah) to full, concrete internal injustice (Israel, by far the longest oracle, 2:6-16, and the only one without a fire-verse); (iii) ch3's own direct, personal address to Israel (3:1-15), opening with unprecedented second-person address ("Hear... against YOU"), arguing via a rhetorical-question chain (3:3-8) that the LORD's judgment — like a lion's roar, like Amos's own prophesying — is never without cause, then closing with specific judgment on Bethel's altars and Israel's own luxury architecture. "Bearing on the inner being" is taken to include: (i) the LORD himself, the controlling voice throughout — his own settled resolve (the "three...four" formula), his past benefactions recalled (2:9, 2:11, 3:1-2), his elective "knowing" of Israel (3:2), and his own necessitating word (3:7-8); (ii) each nation as a corporate collective (Q8), its own crime and disposition (Edom's sustained fratricidal anger, 1:11, being the clearest instance of a foreign nation's own INTERIOR state named as the crime itself); (iii) Israel specifically, both as a corrupted collective (2:6-8's judicial/cultic class) and as the LORD's own elect, uniquely accountable party (3:1-2); (iv) the specific human roles named throughout — the prophets and Nazirites (2:11-12), unnamed office-holders (1:5, 1:15, 2:3), Amos himself (1:1, 3:8); (v) non-human entities whose state bears on human life throughout (the pastures/Carmel, 1:2; the fire as instrument, throughout; the lion/bird/snare analogies, 3:4-5, note b/d).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for all three chapters (184/184, 163/163, 165/165 non-particle spans). Register shifts across the passage: third-person narrative/visionary superscription (1:1) and a first-person-quoted divine roar (1:2); eight repeated third-person "thus says the LORD" oracle-formulas with embedded first-person divine speech (1:3-2:16); a shift to direct second-person address ("Hear... against YOU," 3:1) with first-person divine recollection (3:1-2, 9); a chain of rhetorical questions requiring no named subject (3:3-6) building to an explicit first-person prophetic self-justification (3:7-8); a return to third-person summons-and-witness framing (3:9-13) before a final first-person divine judgment-declaration (3:14-15). Per governance.verse_gap_by_design, three verses in this range have no row in iba.db (Amos 2:10, 2:13, 3:3) and are noted inline at each occurrence, not treated as errors.

**Corpus-continuity check.** No prior filled debate found for this book at or before this range — this is the first debate in the sequence (or nothing precedes it yet). Nothing to re-read.

## Per-verse debate

### Amo 1:1

> The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

**Observation.** "The words [H1697G] of Amos [H5986], who was [H1961] among the shepherds [H5349/H9003] of Tekoa [H8620/H9006], which he saw [H2372] concerning Israel [H3478/H5921A] in the days [H3117G] of Uzziah [H5818G], king [H4428G] of Judah [H3063G], and in the days [H3117G] of Jeroboam [H3379H] the son [H1121A] of Joash [H3101J], king [H4428G] of Israel [H3478], two years before the earthquake [H7494/H9009]."

**Operation 1 — the word coming to be Amos's own, and seen by him.**
- **Action-type:** was/saw (a two-part reception formula — the bare "was" pattern shared with Hosea 1:1/Joel 1:1/Jonah 1:1/Obad 1, PLUS an added act of Amos's own, "which he saw" [H2372, chazah], matching Micah 1:1's own addition rather than Hosea's bare reception).
- **Subject:** Amos — named as the word's recipient and, distinctively, as one who himself "saw" it; identified further by trade (a shepherd of Tekoa) and by two royal reference-points (Uzziah of Judah, Jeroboam of Israel).
- **Operation:** a state (the word simply "was" his) plus a movement of his own (he saw it) — unlike Hosea 1:1's bare reception, Amos is given his own act, however minimal, at the book's very opening.
- **Source:** implicitly the LORD (by continuation of the book's own title-convention; not restated as "the LORD" within this verse itself, contrast v2's explicit naming — a minor structural gap, not filled).
- **Target:** n/a directly within this verse; the word's content begins at v2.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Amos is a focused inner being in his own right, given (unusually for this book's opening-formula genre) his own stated act of seeing, not merely bare reception. The named kings (Uzziah, Jeroboam) and father (Joash) are not candidates — no operation is attributed to any of them; they function solely as a chronological anchor, correctly set aside per step 3 note (a), consistent with the Hosea 1:1 precedent.
- Q3: Both the reception and the seeing are stated explicitly, not inferred.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, by the book's own title-convention (implicit here, explicit at v2); no separate enablement is stated for Amos's own act of seeing.
- Q5: Target = n/a within this verse; content supplied from v2.
- Q6: State (the word "was") and movement (Amos "saw").
- Q7: Forward linkage to the whole book (this verse is the frame within which vv2-3:15 and beyond unfold); also a within-book echo worth flagging (see v2 below) — Amos's own trade as "shepherd" (H5349, ro'eh root) recurs in the very next verse's "pastures of the shepherds" (H7462B, same root family), tying the prophet's own identity to his message's content.
- Q8: N/A this verse (no collective in view beyond the two royal chronological anchors, themselves set aside).
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; nothing about Amos's own interior at the moment of seeing/receiving is given.
- Q11: was/saw.
- Q12: Not applicable this verse (no divine operation stated to compare against).

**Decision.** Retain as the book's formal opening, with Amos's own added act of "seeing" flagged as a point of difference from Hosea's bare-reception opening and a point of likeness to Micah's. The named kings/father are set aside (no operation stated).

### Amo 1:2

> And he said: “The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the top of Carmel withers.”

**Observation.** "And he said [H0559]: 'The LORD [H3068G] roars [H7580] from Zion [H6726/H9006] and utters [H5414M] his voice [H6963A] from Jerusalem [H3389/H9002/H9006]; the pastures [H4999] of the shepherds [H7462B/H9009] mourn [H0056/H9023], and the top [H7218I] of Carmel [H3760G/H9009] withers [H3001].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own roaring/voice, going out from Zion/Jerusalem.**
- **Action-type:** roared/uttered (a lion/thunder image — the book's programmatic epigraph, functioning like a thesis statement for all the judgment-oracles that follow).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a movement — his voice going out from a fixed source (Zion/Jerusalem) to affect the wider created order.
- **Source:** self, explicit, located at Zion/Jerusalem.
- **Target:** the natural order broadly — made concrete in the two following clauses (the shepherds' pastures, Mount Carmel).

**Operation 2 — the shepherds' pastures mourning in response.**
- **Action-type:** mourned.
- **Subject:** "the pastures of the shepherds" — a non-human entity (note (b)) whose state is described in direct relation to a human collective's livelihood (shepherds depend on pasture) — in scope per note (b)/(d), not set aside.
- **Operation:** a state — a stricken condition, responding to Op1's roar.
- **Source:** the LORD's own roar (Op1), by direct causal sequence within the verse.
- **Target:** n/a further; the pastures are themselves the affected party, with the shepherds' livelihood the referential (inferred, note e) human stake.

**Operation 3 — Carmel's own withering.**
- **Action-type:** withered.
- **Subject:** "the top of Carmel" — a fertile, symbolically fruitful mountain (non-human, note (b), its condition standing for the land's own fruitfulness).
- **Operation:** a state, parallel to Op2.
- **Source:** the LORD's roar (Op1), same causal chain.
- **Target:** n/a further.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The LORD is the central active party — an explicit, controlling, judging presence heard from Zion/Jerusalem, prior to and behind every specific oracle that follows. The pastures/Carmel are non-human but their affected state is described in direct relation to human livelihood (note b/d), so retained in scope rather than set aside.
- Q3: All three operations stated explicitly, not inferred.
- Q4: Source throughout = the LORD, self, explicit; the pastures'/Carmel's own stricken states are sourced directly to his roar, not to any other cause.
- Q5: Target = the natural order generally, made concrete as pastures and Carmel — both bearing on human (shepherd) livelihood by inference (note e), not stated directly of a named human party.
- Q6: Movement (the LORD's own roaring/uttering) producing state (the pastures'/Carmel's stricken condition).
- Q7: Forward linkage to the whole book — this verse functions as the thesis the eight nation-oracles (1:3-2:16) and ch3's direct indictment of Israel all instantiate. **Within-book echo, worth flagging distinctly:** v1 names Amos himself "among the shepherds" (H5349, ro'eh root); v2 names "the pastures OF THE SHEPHERDS" (H7462B, same root family) as what mourns under the LORD's roar — the prophet's own trade-vocabulary recurring in the content of what he is given to see, a link between the SPEAKER's own identity and the SPOKEN content, distinct in shape from Q12 (no divine-vs-human operation compared here) and from Hosea's EQ2 self-reversal pattern (no quotation-then-reversal here) — logged as a new emergent-question shape below.
- Q8: The "shepherds" are a human collective (Q8) only by inference from the pastures that are named directly; not itself the grammatical subject of this verse.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: roared/uttered (Op1); mourned (Op2); withered (Op3).
- Q12: Not applicable this verse (all three operations belong to the LORD or to non-human entities responding to him; no human operation is juxtaposed for comparison).

**Decision.** Retain all three operations as the book's programmatic epigraph. The shepherd-vocabulary echo between v1 and v2 is flagged as a new emergent-question shape (speaker-identity ↔ message-content recurrence), distinct from Q12 and from Hosea's self-reversal pattern.

### Amo 1:3

> Thus says the Lord: “For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not revoke the punishment, because they have threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron.

**Observation.** "Thus [H3541] says [H0559] the LORD [H3068G]: 'For three [H7969] transgressions [H6588] of Damascus [H1834], and for four [H0702/H5921A/H9002], I will not [H3808] revoke [H7725O, lit. turn back] the punishment [H5921A, lit. "upon it"], because they have threshed [H1758/H9033/H5921A] Gilead [H1568G/H9009/H0853] with threshing sledges [H2742A/H9048] of iron [H1270/H9009].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own fixed, irrevocable sentence against Damascus.**
- **Action-type:** declared/fixed — a judicial formula: the LORD's own settled, unappeasable resolve, formally announced against a named nation. **This is the book's own structuring device**, repeated with only the nation-name and specific crime varying across all eight oracles (Damascus here; Gaza 1:6; Tyre 1:9; Edom 1:11; Ammon 1:13; Moab 2:1; Judah 2:4; Israel 2:6) — established fully here and cross-referenced, not re-derived from scratch, at each later instance below.
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a state — a declared, fixed judicial disposition ("I will not turn it back"), an interior stance of settled resolve given emphatic numerical form ("three... and for four" — a rhetorical device signalling a full, overflowing measure of guilt, not a literal tally).
- **Source:** self, explicit.
- **Target:** Damascus, the first-named nation in the sequence.

**Operation 2 — Damascus's own committed atrocity, the sentence's stated ground.**
- **Action-type:** threshed (an agricultural-processing verb applied to a war-atrocity — crushing/trampling, here describing brutal treatment of Gilead's population or territory in war).
- **Subject:** Damascus/Syria — a national collective (Q8), the human-relevant agent implied by the nation-name, not further individualised here.
- **Operation:** a movement — a violent act against another collective, already completed (past tense) by the time the oracle is spoken.
- **Source:** self — Damascus's own committed act, not attributed to any enabler.
- **Target:** Gilead (H1568G), a named Israelite region east of the Jordan — the victim collective.
- **Insufficiency:** the specific historical campaign behind "threshed Gilead with sledges of iron" is not detailed in this base extract — named as background the oracle's own accusation presupposes, not supplied from outside knowledge.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Damascus (Q8) is a focused agent whose stated act is given as the cause of the LORD's own disposition (Op1); the LORD's resolve is itself a directly stated interior stance, formally declared rather than left to inference — unusually explicit for the book's first oracle.
- Q3: Both stated explicitly — the crime as plain accusation, the sentence as direct first-person declaration.
- Q4: Source of Damascus's crime = self; source of the LORD's sentence = self — the two kept distinct: Damascus's act is not caused by the LORD, and the LORD's judgment is not caused by anything outside his own resolve. This crime-then-consequence shape runs through all eight oracles.
- Q5: Target of the crime = Gilead (victim); target of the sentence = Damascus (perpetrator).
- Q6: State (the LORD's fixed resolve) and movement (Damascus's already-completed violent act).
- Q7: **Structural linkage, established here for the whole book.** The crime-then-sentence unit (Op1+Op2) recurs, with only nation and crime varying, across all eight oracles (1:3-2:16) — the book's own organising device. Cross-referenced, not re-derived, at each subsequent nation.
- Q8: Damascus/Syria as a national collective — its corporate liability (capable of committing and being held to account for a shared atrocity) reshapes the operation as a movement against/by a NATION.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the specific historical campaign is not detailed here — insufficiency named, not filled.
- Q11: declared/fixed (Op1); threshed (Op2).
- Q12: Not applicable this verse (no human operation juxtaposed against a stated divine act using shared vocabulary within this verse).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Flagged as establishing the book's own two-part oracle-formula (crime + irrevocable sentence), to be cross-referenced, not re-derived, at Gaza/Tyre/Edom/Ammon/Moab/Judah/Israel below.

### Amo 1:4

> So I will send a fire upon the house of Hazael, and it shall devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad.

**Observation.** "So [and] I will send [H7971G] a fire [H0784] upon [in/on/with, H9003] the house [H1004M] of Hazael [H2371], and it shall devour [H0398] the strongholds [H0759H] of Ben-hadad [H1130I]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own act of sending judicial fire.**
- **Action-type:** sent — a decisive, single military-symbolic act giving specific content to v3's declared "punishment."
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a movement, a stated certain future act.
- **Source:** self, explicit.
- **Target:** "the house of Hazael" — the ruling dynasty of Damascus/Syria (Hazael and his son Ben-hadad are historically-attested Syrian kings per the base data's person-notes, 1Ki 19:15/2Ki 13:3) — v3's national target (Damascus broadly) is here narrowed to its ruling house specifically.

**Operation 2 — the sent fire's own devouring.**
- **Action-type:** devoured.
- **Subject:** the fire itself — a non-human agent (note b) acting as the LORD's own instrument.
- **Operation:** a movement.
- **Source:** the LORD, via the sent fire — an enablement relation (Part B.5): the LORD sources the fire's SENDING; the fire then itself acts.
- **Target:** "the strongholds of Ben-hadad" — the dynasty's own fortifications, its material power base.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Hazael and Ben-hadad are named only as designators of "the house of X" — presumptive candidates per step 2 note (f), but here function only as targets, not agents, of their own stated act within this verse.
- Q3: Both stated explicitly.
- Q4: Source of the sending = the LORD, self; source of the devouring = the fire itself, enabled by the LORD (Part B.5 distinction).
- Q5: Target continues and narrows v3's (Damascus generally → its ruling house specifically).
- Q6: Movement throughout.
- Q7: **Second structural device, established here.** Direct linkage back to v3 (the "punishment" there declared is here given content: fire against the ruling house's own strongholds) — this fire/devour/strongholds pattern recurs at every subsequent nation and is cross-referenced, not re-derived, below.
- Q8: The house of Hazael, a dynastic collective narrower than "Damascus" (v3's national collective).
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: sent (Op1); devoured (Op2).
- Q12: Not applicable this verse.

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Flagged, with v3, as jointly establishing the book's two-part oracle-formula (crime+sentence, then fire+strongholds) — cross-referenced at every later nation.

### Amo 1:5

> I will break the gate-bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitants from the Valley of Aven, and him who holds the scepter from Beth-eden; and the people of Syria shall go into exile to Kir,” says the Lord.

**Observation.** "I will break [H7665] the gate-bar [H1280] of Damascus [H1834], and cut off [H3772I] the inhabitants [H3427] from the Valley [H1237J/H9006] of Aven [H0206G], and him who holds [H8551] the scepter [H7626G] from Beth-eden [H1040/H9006]; and the people [H5971A] of Syria [H0758I] shall go into exile [H1540K] to Kir [H7024B], says [H0559/H9011] the LORD [H3068G]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own breaking of Damascus's gate-bar.**
- **Action-type:** broke.
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a movement, continuing vv3-4's sentence.
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** Damascus's own gate-bar — a city-defense feature symbolising the city's capacity to shut out attackers, i.e. its capacity to protect itself.

**Operation 2 — the LORD's own removal of two named office-holders.**
- **Action-type:** cut off.
- **Subject:** the LORD, self; targets are two unnamed administrative figures — "the inhabitant" at the Valley of Aven and "him who holds the scepter" at Beth-eden — each a focused human role (Q1/Q2), though unnamed (referential, note e — the office is named, the person is not).
- **Operation:** a movement.
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** the two office-holders, at two named locations near Damascus.

**Operation 3 — the people of Syria's own exile.**
- **Action-type:** exiled — agency grammatically softer here (a passive-leaning "shall go") than Ops 1-2's direct first-person acts, worth flagging as a minor shift, comparable to Hosea 1:11's own shift in agency.
- **Subject:** "the people of Syria" — a national collective (Q8), resuming v3's Damascus/Syria identity.
- **Operation:** a movement, a stated future deportation.
- **Source:** the LORD, by continuation of the pattern, though the verse's own grammar foregrounds the people's undergoing rather than his direct causing.
- **Target:** n/a further beyond the stated destination (Kir).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The unnamed inhabitant/scepter-holder at Aven/Beth-eden are each presumptive human candidates (an office, even where the person is unnamed) per step 2 note (f); "the people of Syria" is a collective whose own experience of exile is the operation's content.
- Q3: All stated explicitly as the LORD's further judgments; the office-holders' own names are not given — named as referential (note e), not asserted as fact.
- Q4: Source throughout = the LORD, self (Ops 1-2 explicit; Op3's agency grammatically softer but continuing the same source by context).
- Q5: Target of Op1 = Damascus's own defenses; Op2 = the two office-holders; Op3 has no further target beyond the collective's own undergoing.
- Q6: Movement throughout.
- Q7: Direct linkage to vv3-4, continuing and intensifying the same sentence against the same nation. **This verse is Damascus's only oracle with a third elaboration verse beyond the two-verse crime/fire pattern** (contrast Gaza/Tyre/Edom, each shorter) — paralleled only by Ammon's own third verse (1:15) among the eight oracles; flagged in passage-level linkages below.
- Q8: "The people of Syria" — a national collective, its whole population's fate the operation's content.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the identity of the office-holders and Kir's precise location are not further specified — named as background gaps, not filled.
- Q11: broke (Op1); cut off (Op2); exiled (Op3, agency backgrounded).
- Q12: Not applicable this verse.

**Decision.** Retain all three operations. Flagged as the Damascus oracle's own extended third verse — paralleled among the eight oracles only by Ammon's (1:14-15).

### Amo 1:6

> Thus says the Lord: “For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not revoke the punishment, because they carried into exile a whole people to deliver them up to Edom.

**Observation.** "Thus says [H0559/H3541] the LORD [H3068G]: 'For three [H7969] transgressions [H6588] of Gaza [H5804], and for four [H0702/H5921A/H9002], I will not [H3808] revoke [H7725O] the punishment [H5921A], because they carried [H1540K/H9033/H5921A] into exile a whole [H8003] people [H1546/H9048] to deliver them up [H9005/H5462] to Edom [H0123G/H9005].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's fixed sentence against Gaza** (same formula as v3, cross-referenced not re-derived). Subject/Source: the LORD, self. Operation: a state, the same irrevocable resolve. Target: Gaza.

**Operation 2 — Gaza's own committed atrocity: mass deportation of a captive population wholesale ("a whole people," H8003) to Edom for further disposal.** Subject: Gaza (Q8, a Philistine city-state collective). Action-type: exiled/delivered-up — differing in specific content from Damascus's "threshed" (v3): here the crime is trafficking an entire captive population onward to a third party (Edom), compounding the original captivity with a further, mercantile betrayal. Operation: a movement, completed. Source: self. Target: "a whole people" — an unnamed captive collective (referential, note e — their own identity is not given, only their fate), delivered onward to Edom.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Gaza (Q8) is the focused agent of Op2, exactly as Damascus was in v3; the unnamed "whole people" is itself a presumptive human collective (note f) whose own fate (captivity, then re-delivery) is the operation's content, though never named.
- Q3: Stated explicitly throughout.
- Q4: Source of Gaza's own crime = self; source of the LORD's sentence = self — same crime-then-consequence shape as Damascus.
- Q5: Target of Gaza's crime = the unnamed captive people (via Edom, the receiving party); target of the LORD's sentence = Gaza.
- Q6: State (the LORD's resolve) and movement (Gaza's own completed act).
- Q7: Direct instance of the book's own formula (established at vv3-4) — the crime specific to Gaza is a DIFFERENT act from Damascus's (trafficking captives onward, not a battlefield atrocity against a place), while the sentence-structure is identical, underscoring that the "three...four" formula measures a FULL, varied catalogue of distinct national sins, not one repeated offence.
- Q8: Gaza, a Philistine city-state collective; the unnamed "whole people," a captive collective whose own composition is not specified.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the identity of the trafficked "whole people" is not given — named as insufficiency.
- Q11: fixed/declared (Op1); exiled/delivered-up (Op2).
- Q12: Not applicable this verse.

**Decision.** Retain both operations, per the book's established formula (vv3-4).

### Amo 1:7

### Amo 2:4

> Thus says the Lord: “For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not revoke the punishment, because they have rejected the law of the Lord, and have not kept his statutes, but their lies have led them astray, those after which their fathers walked.

**Observation.** "Thus says [H0559/H3541] the LORD [H3068G]: 'For three [H7969] transgressions [H6588] of Judah [H3063G], and for four [H0702/H5921A/H9002], I will not [H3808] revoke [H7725O] the punishment [H5921A], because they have rejected [H3988A/H9033/H5921A] the law [H8451/H9048/H0853] of the LORD [H3068G], and have not [H3808] kept [H8104G/H9023] his statutes [H2706G/H9002], but their lies [H3577/H9038] have led them astray [H8582], those after which [H0310A/H9028] their fathers [H0001G] walked [H1980I/H9028/H0834A].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's fixed sentence against Judah** (book-wide formula, its FIRST application to one of the two covenant nations rather than a foreign power). Target: Judah.

**Operation 2 — Judah's own crime: rejecting the LORD's law and statutes, being led astray by "their lies," walking in an inherited (ancestral) pattern of unfaithfulness.** Subject: Judah (Q8), a covenant nation — a qualitatively different KIND of subject from the preceding six foreign nations, since Judah stands in the SAME covenant relationship to the LORD that Israel (the book's ultimate addressee, ch2:6-3:15) does. Action-type: rejected/not-kept/led-astray. Operation: a movement (rejecting, not keeping — active refusals) PLUS a state (being led astray, a condition Judah is IN, caused by "their lies" — note the SOURCE here is internal to Judah's own tradition, "their lies," not an external nation's violence). Source: self — Judah's own rejection is self-sourced, but the LEADING ASTRAY is sourced to "their lies" (an internal, inherited deceptive tradition — Q4's source-of-enablement distinct from source-of-the-original-rejection) — and further, explicitly, to "their fathers," a THIRD source layer: ancestral practice, inherited rather than freshly originated. Target: the LORD's own law and statutes — the covenant relationship itself, exactly the kind of target Israel's own oracle (2:6-16) will elaborate at length.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Judah (Q8) is a focused covenant-collective; unlike the six foreign nations, Judah's crime is not violence against another nation but an INTERNAL covenant-infidelity — the oracle-cycle's first crime of this qualitatively different kind.
- Q3: Stated explicitly — rejection, non-keeping, and being led astray are all directly declared, not inferred; the ancestral-inheritance framing ("after which their fathers walked") is also stated directly, not inferred.
- Q4: **Three distinct sources named, unusually layered:** (i) Judah's own act of rejecting/not-keeping = self; (ii) the leading-astray = "their lies" (an internal deceptive tradition, distinct from Judah's own direct agency — Part B.5's state-vs-enablement distinction applies unusually clearly here: the LIES enable the astray-condition, while Judah's own will is the site of the original rejection); (iii) the inherited pattern = "their fathers," a THIRD, generational source layer not seen in any of the six foreign-nation oracles.
- Q5: Target = the LORD's own law/statutes — the covenant relationship itself.
- Q6: Movement (rejected, did not keep) and state (led astray, an ongoing condition).
- Q7: **Major structural break from the six preceding oracles.** Every foreign-nation crime (Damascus-Ammon, Moab) was a violent act against ANOTHER NATION or its king; Judah's crime is the cycle's first to be an act (and state) internal to the COVENANT relationship itself — anticipating and directly paralleling Israel's own, far longer oracle (2:6-16) which follows immediately. This is the hinge-point of the whole cycle: the "three... four" formula and fire/strongholds sentence CONTINUE unchanged in form (Op1, v5), but the CONTENT of the accusation shifts registers entirely from international violence to covenant-infidelity — flagged as the cycle's central turn, in passage-level linkages below.
- Q8: Judah, a national covenant-collective — the first of the eight nations addressed as a covenant partner rather than a foreign power.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the specific content of "their lies" is not detailed here (contrast Israel's oracle, which will specify concrete practices) — named as insufficiency, perhaps intentionally brief given Judah's oracle is comparatively short (2 verses) next to Israel's (11 verses, 2:6-16).
- Q11: fixed/declared (Op1); rejected/not-kept/led-astray (Op2).
- Q12: **Possible instance, flagged but not confirmed.** Judah's own "rejecting the law of the LORD" could be read as a human operation standing in some contrast to the LORD's own giving of that law (an implied prior divine operation, not itself stated within this verse) — but since the LORD's own act of giving the law is not itself restated or juxtaposed within THIS verse's own data (only presupposed), this is not a confirmed Q12 instance per the textual-anchoring discipline (Part B.11) — logged as an emergent question instead.

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Flagged as the cycle's central structural turn: the crime-content shifts from international violence (six foreign nations) to covenant-infidelity (Judah, then Israel at greater length) while the oracle-formula itself (Op1) continues unchanged — the clearest evidence that the "three...four" sentence-formula is a fixed FRAME capable of holding qualitatively different kinds of content.

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Flagged as the passage's clearest confirmed Q12 instance and as closing a ring-composition with 1:2 — the book's own opening image (the LORD's roar) is here shown to be the necessitating cause of the prophetic book itself.

- Q11: struck/perished/ended.
- Q12: Not applicable this verse (a wholly divine operation, no human operation compared).

**Decision.** Retain. Flagged as closing the entire Amos 1-3 passage: judgment's final, most concrete content (destroyed luxury-houses) directly answers 2:6-8's own crime-catalogue, completing a crime-to-consequence arc that spans the whole passage and closes the ring-composition opened at 1:2. **Amos 3 (and the whole Amos 1-3 passage) complete at this verse.**

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **The eight-oracle formula (1:3-2:16), established at Damascus (1:3-5) and cross-referenced, not re-derived, at every subsequent nation.** Each oracle shares: (a) "Thus says the LORD: for three transgressions of X, and for four, I will not revoke the punishment, because..." (the fixed judicial sentence, a settled irrevocable resolve); (b) for seven of the eight nations, "so I will send a fire upon..., and it shall devour the strongholds of..." — the fire/strongholds consequence. Verse-count varies (2 verses: Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Judah; 3 verses: Damascus, Ammon, Moab; 11 verses: Israel) independently of crime-length (Edom's crime, v11, is unusually long within a 2-verse oracle) — length and content vary independently.
2. **The crime-content shifts registers partway through the cycle.** Damascus-Ammon-Moab (six nations): international violence against another nation or its king. Judah (2:4-5): the FIRST internal, covenant-infidelity crime (general — "rejected the law"). Israel (2:6-16): the fullest, most concrete internal crimes (specific — selling the poor, corrupting Nazirites/prophets), AND the cycle's only oracle with no fire-verse, replaced instead by the total collapse of every human capacity for strength/courage (vv14-16) — judgment turns from EXTERNAL (city/stronghold destruction) to INTERNAL (the failure of courage itself).
3. **Gilead is victimised twice, by two different perpetrators (Damascus, 1:3; Ammon, 1:13)** — the same victim-region recurring under different national aggressors, distinct from the Gaza/Tyre shared-crime recurrence (same crime, "delivered up a whole people to Edom," charged against two DIFFERENT perpetrators, 1:6/1:9).
4. **Moab's crime (2:1) is against Edom's own king — a nation already itself under judgment (1:11-12) also appears as another nation's victim** — flagged as evidence the LORD's judgment of the nations is comprehensive across every relationship, not only those touching Israel/Judah.
5. **The gift-then-corruption pair (2:11-12): the LORD raises up prophets/Nazirites; Israel directly corrupts both, using the SAME vocabulary in reversed sense** — the passage's single clearest anchored operation-to-operation contrast, proposed as a candidate new category alongside Q12 (divine mirroring) and Hosea's self-reversal pattern.
6. **Three instances of the LORD recalling his own past benefaction as the ground for present accountability**: 2:9 (the Amorite destroyed), 2:11 (prophets/Nazirites raised up), 3:1-2 (the exodus itself, "the whole family... brought up out of Egypt," and the exclusive "knowing" that grounds, rather than mitigates, judgment).
7. **A ring-composition spans the whole passage: 1:2 (the LORD roars) → 3:4/3:8 (the same lion-image explicitly reapplied, and shown to necessitate Amos's own prophesying) → 3:12 (the shepherd/lion image redeployed ironically as "rescue") → 3:15 (the LORD's own agency, explicit, closing the passage).** 3:8 is the passage's clearest CONFIRMED Q12 instance: Amos's own prophetic act is shown, via direct textual anchoring (shared lion-roar vocabulary with 1:2, and direct causal logic — "the LORD has spoken; who can but prophesy?"), to be necessitated by the LORD's own prior operation.
8. **A crime-to-consequence arc spans 2:6-8 (Israel's own economic/cultic corruption) to 3:10-11 (strongholds storing violence, then plundered) to 3:14-15 (Bethel's altars and Israel's luxury-houses destroyed)** — the specific material/cultic sites of Israel's own crimes become judgment's own specific targets, closing the whole passage.
9. **3:9's own reversal: Ashdod (itself judged, 1:6-8) is summoned as a WITNESS against Israel's own worse corruption** — foreign nations once under judgment now serve to confirm the covenant nation's guilt.
10. **The "bow" (H7198) recurs at 2:15 as a failing archer's own weapon** — a cross-book lexical resonance with Hosea 1:5/7's own broken/rejected bow-imagery, logged as an emergent question for eventual cross-book synthesis, not elaborated here.

## Insufficiencies register

1. **The specific historical campaigns behind several crime-clauses are not detailed in this base extract**: Damascus "threshing Gilead" (1:3), the Jehu/Jezreel-type allusions are absent here (unlike Hosea), Tyre's specific "covenant of brotherhood" (1:9), Moab's desecration of Edom's king (2:1) — all named as background the oracles presuppose but do not themselves supply.
2. **The legal/cultic background presupposed by several images is not detailed**: the garment-pledge law behind 2:8 (cf. Exod 22:26-27), the legal-fragment custom behind 3:12's shepherd-analogy (cf. Exod 22:13), the altar-horns' sanctuary-refuge significance behind 3:14 (cf. 1 Kings 1:50-51) — named as presupposed background, not supplied from outside this base extract.
3. **The identity of the unnamed office-holders throughout (Damascus's "inhabitant"/"scepter-holder," 1:5; Ammon's king, 1:15; Moab's "ruler," 2:3; the unnamed "adversary," 3:11) is nowhere given** — named as referential gaps, not filled.
4. **The specific historical referent behind 3:15's "houses of ivory" (likely the Omride dynasty's ivory palace, 1 Kings 22:39) is not itself part of this base extract** — named as probable background, not asserted as this passage's own stated content.
5. **The specific mechanism of Israel's own crimes in 2:6-8 (legal proceeding? outright sale? cultic ritual specifics?) is not further detailed** — named as insufficiency, not inferred.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ1.** Does Q12 (currently scoped to same-passage, textually-anchored divine/human juxtaposition) need to extend to TEMPORAL contrasts — a human's PRESENT conduct measured against the LORD's own PAST benefaction toward that same party (2:9/2:11's benefactions vs. 2:6-8's crimes, and vs. 2:12's direct corruption of the very gifts named in 2:11)? 3:8 supplies a confirmed same-passage Q12 instance (lion-roar/prophesying); 2:9/2:11-12 suggest a related but temporally-structured pattern not yet named. Carried forward for the whole-book read.
- **EQ2.** Is the gift-then-corruption pair (2:11-12, prophets/Nazirites raised up then directly corrupted using shared vocabulary) a distinct category from both Q12 (divine mirroring) and Hosea's self-reversal pattern (the LORD quoting and reversing his OWN prior declaration)? Here it is a HUMAN party (Israel) corrupting what the LORD gave it, not the LORD reversing his own words. Needs its own name if the pattern recurs in later books.
- **EQ3.** Is 3:2/3:10's shared "know" vocabulary (the LORD's own elective "knowing" of Israel, v2; Israel's own failure to "know" how to do right, v10) a deliberate wordplay, or a coincidental recurrence of a common verb? Worth testing against the whole-book read once more of Amos is available.
- **EQ4.** The "bow" (H7198) recurs at 2:15 as a failing archer's own weapon, echoing Hosea 1:5/7's own broken/rejected-bow imagery — a candidate CROSS-BOOK lexical resonance. Per governance, cross-book theme mechanisms are flagged only, not designed/built now — logged here for whenever that mechanism is authorised.
- **EQ5.** Does the shepherd-vocabulary echo between 1:1 (Amos "among the shepherds") and 1:2 ("the pastures of the shepherds mourn") — and its ironic redeployment at 3:12 (the shepherd's own token rescue) — constitute a deliberate authorial device (the prophet's own trade shaping his book's central images), comparable to Hosea's marriage-as-mirror device (Hosea's own EQ1)? Worth watching through the rest of Amos once read.
- **EQ6.** Does Moab's crime against Edom's king (2:1) — one already-indicted nation (Edom) appearing as another's (Moab's) victim — establish a general principle that the LORD's judgment of the nations is comprehensive across every relationship, not only those touching Israel/Judah? Carried forward as a live question for the rest of the book/corpus.
